result.note: Mainly a labour-unrest story. Testing the durable facts on India's LPG import position, Haryana's minimum wage hike and the direction of gas rationing.

questions.prompt: In April 2026, factory workers in Noida protested over rising living costs amid fuel shortages linked to the US-Israeli war on Iran. Consider the following statements:
items: India is the world's second-largest importer of LPG.
In early April 2026, Haryana ordered a 35% hike in minimum wages after unrest in the auto hub of Manesar.
The government cut household cooking gas allocations to protect gas supplies to industry.
questions.ask: How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 3 is wrong. The government cut industrial gas allocations to protect household cooking supplies, which squeezed businesses and workers. Haryana's hike raised its wage floor to INR 19,000 a month, against about INR 13,000 earned by Noida factory workers.
questions.source: The government has cut industrial gas allocations to protect household cooking supplies, squeezing businesses and workers simultaneously.
